content.title: Comment to "aoh4"
content.comment:
${\textbf{Comparison to [a,b]:}}$
First, we have already cited [a] and [b] in our submission:
[a] -> SOFT Lu et al. (2021)
[b] CosFormer Qin et al. (2022)
We have missed [c] and will add it.

We have already compared our method with both [a] and [b] on Tables 1 and 2. 

${\textbf{SwinTrans:}}$
 We show that SimA works with 3 different transformer architectures (DeiT, XCiT, and CvT). We have not done experiments with SwinTrans and do not believe it is necessary or even possible to try all possible architectures exhaustively.

${\textbf{Limited contribution:}}$ We agree that others have used the $\ell_1$ norm in a different way (as stated by the reviewer themselves) and we have cited the ones that we found. However, we strongly disagree that others using the same operation in a different way, limits the novelty of our work.

content.title: Comment to reviewer "6jxc"
content.comment:
${\textbf{How can the replacement from softmax to l1-norm increase the classification accuracy?}}$
We do not claim SimA improves the classification accuracy. It improves run time particularly in edge devices.

${\textbf {Why can single-head attention work well in SimA?}}$
This is described in Section 4.4 and the 2nd paragraph of Section 2.2. Since SimA does $\ell_1$ normalization, the dimensions are more comparable, so one dimension cannot dominate the whole $QK^T$ dot product. Hence, the effect of multiple heads may be less pronounced. 

${\textbf{inference time on edge devices:}}$
 Above Tables (Table 1 and Table 2 in comments[https://openreview.net/forum?id=rSHfAMCc997&noteId=to7sOvL-RB]) show the improvement on some edge devices.

${\textbf{Visualization:}}$
Standard attention passes $QK^T$ through Softmax before multiplying with $V$. However, we multiply $\hat{Q}\hat{K}^T$ directly with $V$. Hence, in our case, the magnitude of $\hat{Q}\hat{K}^T$ should identify which tokens are more important (their information flows to the next layers). The whole point of Fig 3 is to show that this magnitude is correlated with the importance of tokens. We do not expect this to happen for DeiT, so we show the same visualization for DeiT for completeness only.

content.title: Edge Device Comparison
content.comment:
Below is execution time comparison on edge devices: 

We evaluate performance of each model on 3 different devices: Raspberry Pi 4 (Quad core Cortex-A72 @ 1.5GHz), NVIDIA Jetson Nano (Quad-core ARM A57 @ 1.43 GHz), and Apple M1. To measure the effect of $exp(.)$ only, we fix the order of ($QK^TV$) product so that all models have the same dot product complexity. We set $N>D$ in Table1 and $N<D$ in Table 2. We repeat average of the execution time over $1000$ runs. We observe that SimA is faster than other methods, which we believe is due to the increased complexity of $exp(.)$ operation compared to $\ell_1$ normalization on edge devices.


Model |  NVIDIA nano	|   Apple M1   | Rasberry PI 4
-------|-------|--------|-------
SimA   | 63.6 | 20.4 | 51.9
Vanilla Attention   | 144.5 | 26.3 | 160.0
ELU Kernel   | 177.4 | 35.8 | 180.6

Table 1 : N > D : Methods with Linear Attention with respect to D : D = 64, N = 256, H = 8. We report average execution time (ms) for each method over $1000$ run.



Model |  NVIDIA nano	|   Apple M1   | Rasberry PI 4
-------|-------|--------|-------
SimA   | 58.0 | 20.5 | 53.2
XCA  | 144.4 | 36.2 | 178.7
ELU Kernel   | 105.2 | 26.5 | 160.1
SOFT   | 145.9 | 36.0 | 177.4

Table 2 : N < D : Methods with Linear Attention with respect to N: D = 256, N = 64, H = 8 . We report average execution time (ms) for each method over $1000$ run.

content.title: Comments to reviewer "qszN"
content.comment:
${\textbf{Efficient transformers usually employ low-resolution and small token dimensions:}}$
We argue that this should not be the case. It is possible to run transformers in larger resolutions using our method. 

Also, you are right that in low resolution, the improvement is only 10%. However, that is for a regular GPU. Above Tables (Table 1 and Table 2 in comments[https://openreview.net/forum?id=rSHfAMCc997&noteId=to7sOvL-RB]) shows that on edge devices, our method has a much better performance boost even on low resolutions. We believe exp(.) operation is more expensive on edge devices due to limited resources, so our method has more improvement.

We will cite Metaformer.

content.title: Comment to Reviewer "3c8e"
content.comment:
${\textbf{Why it works:}}$
We have provided our intuition in the 2nd paragraph of Section 2.2. In short, in ViT, one dimension can have a very large magnitude and dominate the whole Q^TK dot product rendering other dimensions useless. This may be the reason why multi-head attention outperforms single head since a single dimension can dominate its own head only and not the others. Our $\ell_1$ normalization is an extreme case where the number of heads is large.

${\textbf{The same strategy can also be applied to NLP tasks}}$
We do not believe our method is specific to vision transformers only, but since we do computer vision research, we have not done any experiment for NLP or other domains, so we do not have any results.

${\textbf{Why faster if the FLOPS do not change?}}$
The whole idea is that exp(.) operation is expensive, so we are eliminating this operation. Although we do not change the total FLOPS, since exp(.) is eliminated, our model runs faster particularly on edge devices. We have done some experiments on edge devices that are shown in above Tables (Table 1 and Table 2 in comments[https://openreview.net/forum?id=rSHfAMCc997&noteId=to7sOvL-RB])

${\textbf{How about ViT:}}$
We experiment with a variation of DeiT that does not have any distillation, so it is considered to be almost the same as ViT.

${\textbf{Visualization:}}$
Standard attention passes $QK^T$ through Softmax before multiplying with $V$. However, we multiply $\hat{Q}\hat{K}^T$ directly with $V$. Hence, in our case, the magnitude of $\hat{Q}\hat{K}^T$ should identify which tokens are more important (their information flows to the next layers). The whole point of Fig 3 is to show that this magnitude is correlated with the importance of tokens. We do not expect this to happen for DeiT, so we show the same visualization for DeiT for completeness only.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a softmax-free attention operation for a vision Transformer. In practice, the simple L_1 norm is employed to replace softmax to normalize query and key matrices. In addition, a dynamic mechanism is introduced to adjust the multiplication ordering of the query, the key, and the value matrices to reduce the computational cost at the inference phase. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed SimA for various Transformer architectures on numerous basic computer vision tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 
+ The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
+ Accelerating the inference speed of the Transformer is critical in real applications, and the proposed SimA has addressed such an issue from a practical perspective.
+ The performance seems great.

Weakness
- How about the performance (both the accuracy and speed) compared with the other softmax-free attention operations, such as [a,b]?
- Since SwinTrans is a more popular architecture for vision tasks, especially the dense prediction task, how about the performance of the proposed SimA applying to SwinTrans?
- The proposed SimA seems to be a simple solution to save the computation cost of a Transformer in real applications. However,  the L_1 norm has already been applied in previous architecture [c] and the following applications. Even though their purposes differ from this paper, using the L_1 norm to normalize the K, Q, and V in attention operation to reduce their value scales is not novel in the literature. From my perspective, the pure technique contribution of this paper is limited.

[a] Lu J, Yao J, Zhang J, Zhu X, Xu H, Gao W, Xu C, Xiang T, Zhang L. SOFT: softmax-free transformer with linear complexity. NeurIPS 2021

[b] Qin Z, Sun W, Deng H, Li D, Wei Y, Lv B, Yan J, Kong L, Zhong Y. cosFormer: Rethinking Softmax in Attention. ICLR2022

[c] Guo, M.H., Liu, Z.N., Mu, T.J. and Hu, S.M., 2022. Beyond self-attention: External attention using two linear layers for visual tasks. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written, and the idea is straightforward. The idea makes sense and is critical in real applications, and the paper is reproducible, but the pure technique contribution is still limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: Accelerating the inference speed of the Transformer is critical in real applications, and the proposed SimA has addressed such an issue from a practical perspective. Some novel architectures and relevant softmax-free attention operations are suggested to use for comparison in the paper. Since using the L_1 norm to reduce the value scale has already been fully discussed in previous articles, the pure technique contribution seems still limited.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces a new softmax-free self-attention layer called SimA. The core idea of the method is to replace softmax operation with channel-wise l1-normalization so that the heavy cost of softmax can be removed. In addition, the computation order of Q, K, and V can be optionally changed to reduce $O(DN^2)$ to $O(D^2N)$. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in various vision tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The experimental results are powerful in that the proposed SimA achieves higher accuracy with faster inference. Although the idea is simple, the authors presented the advantage of the method thoroughly.
- It is interesting finding that single-head attention / ReLU variants can achieve comparable performance. Also, it is very impressive that there was no instability issue.

Weaknesses:
- The (intuitive) explanation about the performance improvement is somewhat weak. In other words, the authors would answer these questions: How can the replacement from softmax to l1-norm increase the classification accuracy? Why can single-head attention work well in SimA?
- It would be great if Tables include not only FLOPs but also (relative) inference time, as measured in Figure 1. 
- Minor: the motivation is especially critical for edge devices, but there is no related experiment. I understand that the full network implementation is very difficult; however, comparing a small part (ex: query-key dot product) on edge environments will strengthen the paper’s importance.
- Minor: it is difficult to understand the meaning of visualization (Figure 3). Is it correctly catching the object? Please consider revising it.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and easy to follow. Replacing softmax with l1-norm itself is simple but efficient. As I am aware, this is the first to adopt l1-norm in ViT. The authors also provided a code for the paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the paper presents a simple idea and verifies its usefulness with extensive experiments. I don’t think simplicity should be penalized. However, I hope the authors can provide some intuition about the proposed method.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper introduced SimA, a simple attention block that does not involve exp(.) operation, to reduce the computational cost of transformers.

SimA performs normalization on key and query matrices before multiplying them, enabling dynamically switching between O(DN^2) or
O(D^2 N) depending on the number of tokens. 

Extensive experiments show that while reducing the cost of inference, SimA achieves on-par results compared to SOTA methods on various benchmarks including ImageNet classification, MS-COCO object detection and segmentation, and self-supervised learning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

(1) Removing the exp() step can significantly improve the efficiency of the transformer.

(2) The proposed SimA achieves sota performance on the tasks of ImageNet classification, COCO detection&segnmentation.

Weakness:

(1) Efficient transformers usually employ low-resolution and small token dimensions. In Tab 1, there is significant efficiency improvement when resolution is 1536x1536, and the token dimension is 16384. The efficiency improvement for 512x512 resolution and 2048 token dimension is just around 10%.

(2) DeiT, XCiT and CvT are published in 2021. It is better to include some work published in 2022, such as metaformer.

Yu, Weihao, Mi Luo, Pan Zhou, Chenyang Si, Yichen Zhou, Xinchao Wang, Jiashi Feng, and Shuicheng Yan. "Metaformer is actually what you need for vision." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pp. 10819-10829. 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The motivation of this paper is clear. Removing the exp() step can improve the efficiency of the transformer.
This is a practical research work with code released. Thus, it can be easily reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed SimA attention block does not use Softmax, which makes it computationally efficient. SimA can dynamically choose to be linear on N or D at the test time depending on the image resolution or the number of tokens.  The proposed SimA is simple and effective for image classification, object detection and segmentation. However, the acceleration ratio for the proposed method is not significant and the methods used for comparison are too old.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposed a simple solution to replace the softmax operation in vision transformers. It can be achieved by replacing it with $L_1$
norm on the query and key matrices. Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet dataset for image classification and MS-COCO for object detection and semantic segmentation. The results show that the proposed solution is competitive with other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weakness:

1. The proposed solution is indeed very simple, however, the performance degenerates as expected. Also, I could not find any changes in the parameters and the Flops of the modified networks. Why this modified network is faster than others while all the flops remain the same? Moreover, the authors should provide the actual throughput of each model to reflect the actual speed differences. Otherwise, we could not justify the speed.

2. The paper lacks an analysis of the proposed method. All we can see here is by replacing the exp with normalization can speed up and the performance is affected as well. However, for a top-tier ml conference paper, rather than knowing the results, we would like to know why we can do it in this way. In other words, with that many linear attention variants, why we can simply discard the exp operation and replace it with normalization can achieve comparable performance? Does it mean that other linear attentions are doing it in the wrong way? The same strategy can also be applied to NLP tasks and the LRA benchmark as well? If not, why it is working in vision transformers? I think it is much more important than just providing the results on several datasets. 

3. The visualization of the heatmap could not provide useful information. I can see that the heatmap from DeiT is noisier than the SimA， however, the results show that the DeiT actually provides higher accuracy than the SimA.  How to explain that?

4. The author only replaces the exp with SimA in several transformer variants. How about the ViT? I need to know if it is a universal solution for transformer structures.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The implementation of the proposed method should be easy.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The significance of the proposed method should be justified. By replacing the softmax with the l1 norm, the performance degenerates. There is no drop in either parameters or Flops as well. With the lack of actual throughput, I could hardly justify the benefits of using this solution. Also, the proposed method lies behind several linear variants as well, i.e., SOFT. 

More important is that I would like to know why this solution is working in vision transformers. And this paper does not provide sufficient analysis of it.

content.title: SimA: Simple Softmax-free Attention For Vision Transformers
content.TL;DR: SimA is a simple softmax-free and hardware friendly attention that has on-par accuracy with SOTA vision transformers.
content.abstract: Recently, vision transformers have become very popular. However, deploying them in many applications is computationally expensive partly due to the Softmax layer in the attention block. We introduce a simple yet effective, Softmax-free attention block, SimA, which normalizes query and key matrices with simple $\ell_1$-norm instead of using Softmax layer. Then, the attention block in SimA is a simple multiplication of three matrices, so SimA can dynamically change the ordering of the computation at the test time to achieve linear computation on the number of tokens or the number of channels. We empirically show that SimA applied to three SOTA variations of transformers, DeiT, XCiT, and CvT, results in on-par accuracy compared to the SOTA models, without any need for Softmax layer. Interestingly, changing SimA from multi-head to single-head has only a small effect on the accuracy, which further simplifies the attention block.
